# Hillerød: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge

Hillerød: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge is a child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinic (børne- og ungdomspsykiatrisk ambulatorium) reporting into the Danish national ADHD quality registry, the ADHD-databasen [^src1]. It is listed under [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] across multiple years of reporting [^src1] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src9], making it one of the region's designated units for diagnosing and treating ADHD in children and young people.

The clinic appears repeatedly in the ADHD-databasen's annual reports, which track quality indicators for ADHD diagnosis and treatment across Denmark's five regions. In the report covering the period 01.04.2023–31.03.2024, Hillerød's most notable reported figure is its performance on **Indikator 3** — a measure of diagnostic conferences held within 120 days of assessment start — where the clinic achieved 27% fulfilment (95% CI 24-31) across 138 of 504 assessment pathways. This is reflected directly in the underlying claim: Hillerød: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge opnåede 27 % opfyldelse af Indikator 3 blandt 504 udredningsforløb [^src3]. This places Hillerød well below the 90% national development target described for this indicator, a shortfall the broader report attributes to system-wide pressures including staffing shortages and rising referral volumes [^src3].

The clinic also reported on **Indikator 4** (coordinating network meetings within 90 days of treatment start). One tabulation records: Hillerød havde 25 % opfyldelse af indikator 4 (95% CI: 20-31) med 63 forløb ud af 248 [^src1]. A separate 2023 entry shows a different cohort with 0% fulfilment across 117 of 248 pathways [^src2]. On somatic examination reporting, Hillerød recorded 406 of 504 pathways (81%) with documented somatic assessment [^src6]. A further 2023 entry shows 11 of 44 pathways with 0% on one measure and 25% (95% CI 13-40) on another [^src4].

In the subsequent report covering 01.04.2024–31.03.2025, the clinic (identified there as "Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge, Hillerød, B39") continues to show mixed results across several indicators: 147 of 436 pathways at 34% [^src7]; 80 of 474 at 17% (95% CI 14-21) [^src8]; 122 of 431 at 28% (95% CI 24-33) [^src9]; 212 of 431 at 49% (95% CI 44-54) [^src10]; and 296 of 431 at 69% (95% CI 64-73) with a 0% sub-figure noted [^src10]. Smaller cohorts appear in later tables, including 0 of 5 (0%, 95% CI 0-52) [^src11], 3 of 5 (60%, 95% CI 15-95) [^src12], a raw count of 7 [^src13], and 0 of 3 (0%, 95% CI 0-71) [^src14].

Taken together, these figures place Hillerød among the many Danish child and adolescent psychiatric units that the ADHD-databasen reports as falling substantially short of the 90% development targets set for most indicators — a pattern the underlying reports link to a pressured child and adolescent psychiatric system, long waiting times, and prioritisation of assessment over follow-up interventions such as psychoeducation and network coordination.
